newsitem.title: INDIA: India's Kashmir state to release 450 detainees.
newsitem.headline: India's Kashmir state to release 450 detainees.

text.p: India's Jammu and Kashmir state has pledged to release 450 people detained on suspicion of having links with separatist guerrillas, a government spokesman said on Monday.
"In keeping with the assurance held out by Chief Minister Farooq Abdullah, the government have decided to release 450 detenus (detainees) shortly," the spokesman said.

The federal government, which imposed direct rule in the state in 1990 after a bloody rebellion erupted, has used its sweeping anti-terrorist laws to detain people suspected of having links to separatist rebels, often holding them without trial.
"All the 450 were directly or indirectly connected with millitancy," the state government spokesman said, referring to the armed rebellion in mainly Hindu India's only Moslem majority state.
Abdullah, who took office last month after the first local elections in Jammu and Kashmir since the separatist revolt began, had promised he would release all detainees found innocent.
Officials said the release would be based on the recommendations of a government screening committee.
Indian authorities say more than 2,400 Kashmiri separatists or supporters are in various Indian jails but separatists say there are more than 10,000.
In another development, at least 144 militants surrendered their weapons on Monday to Abdullah, police said.
"I congratulate you all who have surrendered your arms, and I hope you will join us in the reconstruction of Jammu and Kashmir state," Abdullah told the militants.
Huddled together in a small tent near a Srinagar jail, the militants came one by one and handed over their weapons to Abdullah, who blessed each of the militants.
But the All-Parties' Hurriyat Conference, which groups 30 separatist groups, described the event as a stage-managed affair.
"The surrender is stage-managed, it is fake. These are pro-government militants who surrendered their weapons and later they get their arms back," a Hurriyat spokesman told Reuters.
More than a dozen militant groups are fighting New Delhi's rule in Jammu and Kashmir. Police and hospitals say more than 20,000 people have been killed in the nearly seven-year-old rebellion.
